$comment: One rule, two languages: which thinking levels a model offers, and which one a stored setting keeps against it. `thinking_levels`/`keep_level` in `src-tauri/src/settings/mod.rs` and `thinkingLevelsFor`/`keepThinkingLevel` in `src/models/settings.ts` are the same arithmetic written twice, and until this file they were held together by a prose comment in each saying the other agreed. Both suites read every row here, so a divergence is a failing test rather than a stored setting quietly downgraded on the next save.
$scopeComment: Not `piThinkingLevel` in `scripts/thinking-level.mjs`, which answers a different question: what a chosen level is called in pi's own effort vocabulary at request time. Its mandatory fallback looks like this rule and is not one — it picks out of the model's own list rather than out of the offered set, and it answers `medium` where this answers `off`, because `off` is not a thing a mandatory model can be sent.
$orderComment: `kept` falls back to the cheapest level the model still offers, cheapest by the ascending EFFORT_LEVELS order and never by the model's own list — OpenRouter answers ["max", "high", "low"], and taking the first of that would answer a stored request for no thinking with the most expensive setting there is.

rows.name: a model that does not reason offers nothing but off
a model that names its own levels offers those, with off in front
a model that must reason drops off from what it offers
a model that takes an effort but names no levels offers the whole scale
a model that must reason and names no levels offers the scale without off
a template with a place for thinking and no effort to name is on or off
the same template, when thinking cannot be turned off, is on and nothing else
